rappel_detail.notes: A free-hanging rappel of about 140 ft to the saddle with two ropes, then scramble down the drainage to the base. A single 70 m rope also works if you accept about 15 ft of easy downclimbing at the bottom.
rappel_detail.anchor: bolts on west side of summit
hazards: single-rope option leaves a short downclimb
rappel_detail.station: Find the rappel anchors on the west side of the summit.

ab_whiteman_falls_drainage_ice_mixed_whi.rappels: Two rappels normally; a single one is possible with a pair of 70 m ropes when snow has accumulated below.

wa_winter_spring_ice_snow_mixed_2_east_f.rappel_count_note: Descends via The Tooth's shared South Face rap line; reported as ~4 rappels combining upper tree/gear anchors with two bolted chain stations lower down near Pineapple Pass (one party describes 4 raps on one rope, or 2 on twin ropes, with sling anchors on trees/boulders). Individual per-station lengths beyond the ~4-rap, single-60m-rope total aren't known, so no per-station length is shown.

wa_winter_spring_ice_snow_mixed_2_northe.rappels: Standard descent follows the South Face rappel line (4 raps, roughly 25-30m each) back to Pineapple Pass; some winter parties instead make 2 long rappels (60m) from a tree below the summit directly down to the notch before skiing out.
wa_winter_spring_ice_snow_mixed_2_northe.rappel_count_note: Four rappels on a single 60 m rope, each under 30 m, reversing the four pitches of the South Face - this is the standard descent that Northeast Slabs parties join at the summit. Two 60 m ropes let you link them into fewer, longer raps. A separate two-rappel option exists in the east gully off Pineapple Pass on two bolted chain stations (60 m rope); its second station is not directly below the first, so you rappel out east and may have to scramble a few feet up a rib to reach it - that is a different line, not part of the four-rappel tree sequence above. Some winter parties instead take two long 60 m rappels from a tree below the summit straight down to the notch.
wa_winter_spring_ice_snow_mixed_2_northe.descent_text: From the summit, downclimb a short distance to the tree anchor in the small notch just below the true summit. From there, rappel the South Face line to the notch (Pineapple Pass) between The Tooth and its south sub-summit — four rappels of under 30 m on a single 60 m rope, or two long ones with two 60 m ropes; parties often note the second rappel can pull stiffly, so flake the rope and check your pull direction before committing. Some parties instead rappel off a chockstone lower on the gully, but this is described as less efficient than the tree-anchor double rappel and is not the standard line. From the notch you join the South Face (standard) descent: downclimb/walk the gully and talus down through Great Scott Bowl, then retrace the approach traverse back above Source Lake to the Snow Lake/Source Lake trail and the Alpental lot. In good winter/spring coverage this whole descent from the notch is frequently skied or glissaded — parties report as little as ~10 minutes from the notch back to the car on skis in prime conditions; on foot through talus, plan on more like 45-60 minutes. The same avalanche exposure noted on the approach applies to the descent, and expect possible traffic from parties climbing the South Face route if your lines overlap near Pineapple Pass.
